analysis.title: US Flash: Blue Wave Crushes Trump's MAGA
key_insights: Democrats won control of both houses of Congress at the midterm elections. Berenberg says the swing against Trump and MAGA was bigger than expected.
Berenberg expects gridlock on US domestic legislation. Trump becomes a lame duck for his final two years but could probably still veto Democratic initiatives.
Berenberg expects both parties to lift the debt ceiling when required, after some brinkmanship, and to avoid protracted government shutdowns. Gridlock will likely prevent new fiscal stimulus.
Berenberg expects US GDP growth to slow towards about 1.5% in 2028. The drivers are slower AI investment growth, the drag from the immigration clampdown, and no new fiscal stimulus.

Congress controls laws but not federal regulations, so the federal regulatory approach may not change. The vote could still affect business decisions in sectors seen as favoured by Trump, such as fossil fuels and AI.
Democrats may use state-level gains to tighten state regulations, potentially including higher hurdles for some data centre investments.

Berenberg expects Democrats to subpoena Trump allies and possibly start impeachment procedures against cabinet officials or Trump. Conviction would need a two-thirds Senate majority, so Berenberg sees it as probably futile.

Berenberg says a lame-duck Trump remains commander in chief and may pursue more geopolitical adventures. Congress will most likely not fund an expensive campaign like the Iran war, but Cuba may have to worry.

Berenberg expects mounting pressure from Republicans on Trump to resolve the Iran issue and bring petrol prices down. It expects an explicit or implicit deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz by early 2027, with or without a final round of bombing in the next few weeks.
Berenberg's forecasts assume Brent falls to $75 per barrel by end-2027 and averages $65 in 2028.
Berenberg treats Trump pressuring Ukraine into de facto surrender as a tail risk rather than a likely outcome, because Trump's influence over Republicans will likely wane after the defeat.
Berenberg sees Jon Ossoff as the early favourite for the 2029 presidency, citing electionbettingodds. It describes him as a centrist, and cautions that early favourites do not always win.

sector_views.rationale: Business decisions in sectors seen as favoured by Trump, including fossil fuels, could be affected as the political pendulum swings against Trump policies.
AI investment growth is expected to slow, and Democratic-led states may raise hurdles for some data centre investments.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Gridlock blocking new fiscal stimulus, slower AI investment growth and the immigration clampdown slow US growth, so the US contributes less to global growth.
Assumes a US-Iran deal reopens the Strait of Hormuz by early 2027 and eases oil prices.
Berenberg's forecast assumes oil prices fall further after the Hormuz reopening.

risk_factors: Potential for more regulation, including state-level regulation, after the Democratic swing.
Foreign policy escalation by a lame-duck Trump, including a possible new round of bombing in Iran and action on Cuba.
Trump pressuring Ukraine into a deal on Russian terms, which would raise refugee flows and European defence spending.
Persistent high petrol prices that the Iran conflict and Hormuz closure keep in place until a deal is reached.
Gridlock over the debt ceiling and government shutdowns.
geopolitical: Democrats won both houses of Congress at the US midterm elections, making Trump a lame duck.
Berenberg expects Trump to strike an explicit or implicit deal with Iran that reopens the Strait of Hormuz by early 2027, possibly after a final round of bombing in the coming weeks.
Berenberg says such a deal would probably be closer to Iranian terms than the initial US and Israeli objectives, and probably worse than the 2015 nuclear accord.
Berenberg says Cuba may have to worry about foreign policy actions by a lame-duck Trump.

Berenberg sees Trump pressuring Ukraine to concede to Russian demands as a tail risk. Europe, led by Germany, would step up support but cannot fully replace US intelligence, satellite access and interceptor missiles.

key_data_points.context: Slowdown driven by AI investment growth, immigration clampdown and no new fiscal stimulus.
key_data_points.anchor: this will dampen US GDP growth towards a pace of c1.5% in 2028

key_data_points.context: Premised on a Trump deal with Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz by early 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Berenberg's chief economist views the voters' rejection of Trump as a sign US institutions and checks and balances work, which is positive.
tension_points.bear_case: In parts of financial markets, the size of the swing could raise concerns about more regulation to come, including tighter state rules on data centres.

tension_points.bull_case: Republican pressure over petrol prices leads Trump to a deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz by early 2027, and Brent falls to $75 by end-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: A new round of bombing may come first, and the deal would probably be closer to Iranian terms and worse than the 2015 accord.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz by early 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: Political gridlock will likely prevent a new fiscal stimulus and slow US growth.
theme_stances.evidence: political gridlock will likely prevent a new fiscal stimulus

theme_stances.key_argument: Pressure from Republicans over petrol prices will push Trump towards a deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz by early 2027.
